title: Reverse Nodes in Even Length Groups
summary: Given a linked list, nodes are sequentially grouped into lengths following the sequence of natural numbers (1, 2, 3, 4, ...).
statement: Given a linked list, nodes are sequentially grouped into lengths following the sequence of natural numbers (1, 2, 3, 4, ...). Reverse the nodes within each group that has an even length, and return the head of the modified linked list. The length of the last group may be shorter than or equal to the length of the second-to-last group.
constraints: Partition nodes consecutively into requested sizes one, two, three, and so on; the final group may be shorter.
Reverse a group exactly when its actual node count is even.
Return the resulting linked-list head using constant auxiliary pointer space.
hints: First measure each actual group; the shortened final group’s parity is what matters.
Keep a pointer before the group, find its tail and length, and reverse exactly that many links when the length is even.
Reverse with after-group as the initial previous pointer, reconnect before.next, then advance before to the old first node.
The reconnection preserves the rest of the list, and each node is visited by one measurement plus at most one reversal.
editorial: The reconnection preserves the rest of the list, and each node is visited by one measurement plus at most one reversal.

tests.explanation: Groups have actual sizes 1,2,3,4; reversing groups two and four gives [5,6,2,3,9,1,4,8,3,7].
The final group has one node, so only the second group is reversed.
